name: Kendrick Lamar
description:
'''Kendrick Lamar Duckworth''' (born June 17, 1987) is an American rapper and songwriter. Rooted in [[West Coast hip-hop]], his music features [[conscious rap|conscious]], introspective lyrics, with [[political criticism]] and [[social commentary]] concerning [[African-American culture]]. [[Music journalists]] have listed Lamar among the greatest rappers of all time. In 2018, he became the first musician outside of the [[Classical music|classical]] and [[jazz]] genres to receive the [[Pulitzer Prize for Music]].

Born and raised in [[Compton, California]], Lamar began releasing music under the stage name '''K.Dot''' in [[Secondary school|high school]]. He signed with [[Top Dawg Entertainment]] (TDE) in 2005 and co-founded the hip hop [[Supergroup (music)|supergroup]] [[Black Hippy]]. His [[Alternative hip-hop|alternative rap]] debut album, ''[[Section.80]]'', led to a joint contract with [[Dr. Dre]]'s [[Aftermath Entertainment]] and [[Interscope Records]]. ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' ranked his next albums ''[[Good Kid, M.A.A.D City]]'' (2012), ''[[To Pimp a Butterfly]]'' (2015), and ''[[Damn (album)|Damn]]'' (2017) among the [[Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Albums of All Time|greatest albums of all time]]. In 2018, he curated [[Black Panther: The Album|the soundtrack]] to the film ''[[Black Panther (film)|Black Panther]]''. Its single "[[All the Stars]]" earned him a nomination for the [[Academy Award for Best Original Song]]. His fifth album, ''[[Mr. Morale & the Big Steppers]]'' (2022), and  [[Drake–Kendrick Lamar feud|feud]]-inspired sixth album, ''[[GNX (album)|GNX]]'' (2024), each debuted atop the US [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]]. He has six US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] number-one singles: "[[Bad Blood (Taylor Swift song)|Bad Blood]]" (as a featured artist), "[[Humble (song)|Humble]]", "[[Like That (Future, Metro Boomin and Kendrick Lamar song)|Like That]]", "[[Not Like Us]]", "[[Squabble Up]]", and "[[Luther (Kendrick Lamar song)|Luther]]".

[[List of awards and nominations received by Kendrick Lamar|Lamar's accolades]] include 27 Grammy Awards—the [[Grammy Award milestones#Most Grammys won by a rapper|most for a rapper]]—2 [[Primetime Emmy Awards]], a [[Brit Awards|Brit Award]], 5 [[American Music Awards]], 7 [[Billboard Music Awards|''Billboard'' Music Awards]], 11 [[MTV Video Music Awards]] and a record 37 [[BET Hip Hop Awards]]. ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' listed him as one of the [[Time 100|100 most influential people in the world]] in 2016. Three of his works were included in ''[[Rolling Stone]]''{{'}}s 2020 revision of the "[[Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Albums of All Time|500 Greatest Albums of All Time]]". In 2025, he headlined the most-watched [[Super Bowl LIX halftime show|Super Bowl halftime show]] in history, while his [[Grand National Tour]] with [[SZA]] became the highest-grossing co-headlining tour of all time. Outside of music, Lamar co-founded the creative company [[PGLang]] and ventured into film with his longtime creative partner, [[Dave Free]].
